state.claim: People who do not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the 2020 elections will not get the COVID vaccine free of cost.

candidates.quote: India has seen a downturn in new coronavirus cases after peaking last month at nearly 100,000 confirmed infections per day. India is still reporting some 50,000 daily cases. In eastern Bihar state, the party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi has promised residents free doses of a future coronavirus vaccine — but only if the party wins in the November 10 elections. Opposition parties blasted the move, saying Modi’s party is exploiting the pandemic for political gain.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav welcomed Centre's decision to give free vaccines to states

Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday welcomed the Centre's decision to provide free vaccines to states for all above 18 years starting June 21, and asked people to get themselves vaccinated,

In a tweet in Hindi, Mr Yadav said, "Seeing the public outrage, the government instead of politicising the corona vaccine announced that it would give the vaccines doses. We were against the BJP's vaccine but welcome the vaccine of Government of India. I will also get vaccinated. I appeal to those who could not get vaccinated for the lack of vaccines to do so."
The BJP's Uttar Pradesh unit had described it as a "good message", and said Samajwadi Party workers and its president should take inspiration from him.

passages.P3: ## COVID-19 Vaccine India: Akhilesh Yadav had earlier triggered a controversy by saying he will not get himself injected with a "BJP vaccine" against coronavirus.
passages.P5: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav welcomed Centre's decision to give free vaccines to states
passages.P7: Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday welcomed the Centre's decision to provide free vaccines to states for all above 18 years starting June 21, and asked people to get themselves vaccinated,
passages.P8: Taking a swipe at Mr Yadav for his remarks, UP BJP media co-convenor Navin Srivastava said it is "better late than never".
passages.P9: In a tweet in Hindi, Mr Yadav said, "Seeing the public outrage, the government instead of politicising the corona vaccine announced that it would give the vaccines doses. We were against the BJP's vaccine but welcome the vaccine of Government of India. I will also get vaccinated. I appeal to those who could not get vaccinated for the lack of vaccines to do so."
passages.P10: In an address to the nation on Monday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced that the central government will provide free vaccines to states for all above 18 years starting June 21.
passages.P11: When the coronavirus vaccine was launched in January, Akhilesh Yadav had sought to know from the government how the drive will be conducted and when the poor will get the shot free of cost.
passages.P12: The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister had said he has faith in doctors of the country but not the government.
passages.P13: Reacting to his fresh remarks, Mr Srivastava said,"Seeing the public outrage, will get the vaccine administered, which has become the vaccine of India from BJP's vaccine. Better late than never".
passages.P14: Akhilesh Yadav had earlier triggered a controversy by saying he will not get himself injected with a "BJP vaccine" against coronavirus.
passages.P15: Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav had got himself vaccinated at a private hospital in Lucknow on Monday.
passages.P16: The BJP's Uttar Pradesh unit had described it as a "good message", and said Samajwadi Party workers and its president should take inspiration from him.
